title: bug: declare_files cannot land a peer-contested path that was dirty at the landing session's pre-flight, so a governor's attribution of stranded bytes is silently held
description:
Observed 2026-10-26. V02 (task-23a5563c) worker completion b7a9bb5 reported `held=docs/MCP_SERVER.md(task-7a0b1881)`. Its +14/-4 doc hunk stayed dirty because parked peer 7a0b1881 (BLOCKED, unassigned) also declares the file. The governor verified the diff was V02's alone and ran `moe.declare_files {taskId: V02, paths: [docs/MCP_SERVER.md]}`, the remedy governor.md prescribes for stranded paths. The next landing would still have held it: QA had to make a byte-neutral Edit-tool touch so the path entered TOOL, and only then did QA checkpoint 66ef204 land it.

Mechanism (scripts/moe-agent.sh resolve_attribution, around line 3634, with a ps1 twin): for a path in MINE that is also in PEER, contested_policy 'skip-untouched' lands it only if `pk in TOOL` or `idle_clean` (clean at this session's pre-flight AND every contesting peer idle). DECLARED is consulted only after that check, so declare_files never overrides the hold. The safety reason is sound: a path that was dirty at pre-flight may carry the peer's unlanded hunks.

The gap: the documented remedy (scripts/CLAUDE.md: declare_files paths are "committed regardless of baseline"; governor.md cheat sheet: declare_files onto the owner "so its next exit lands them") silently does nothing for a contested path. The held= banner gives no hint, so the bytes strand until some session happens to touch them.

Options for the planner, not prescriptive: (a) let a declare_files entry land a contested path when every contesting peer is idle (the peer-idle signal already exists), keeping the hold for live peers; (b) keep the code as-is, but have the held= banner and the record_commit #governors alert name the working remedy (an editing-tool touch in the owner's next session, or finishing/unblocking the peer), and fix the docs. Whichever you choose, the two wrappers must match.
definitionOfDone: A path the owner task declared via declare_files, contested only by idle peers, is either landed by the owner's next exit, or the held=/#governors output names the remedy that works. Which of the two is a recorded planning decision.
A path contested by a LIVE peer (active assignee, open attempt or recent attempt-phase change) is still held, as today. No change can land a live peer's in-flight hunks.

scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 behave identically. bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh pass, with a regression case for a declared, dirty-at-pre-flight, idle-peer-contested path.
scripts/CLAUDE.md (Land on every exit) and docs/roles/governor.md describe declare_files' interaction with contested paths accurately.

Idle does not prove pre-existing dirty bytes are ours; declare_files must not silently override the hold. Reporting must distinguish actual skipped paths from contested trailers (which can accompany a landed TOOL path). planningNotes.risks: No new permission to land active/unknown peers. Existing TOOL and clean-at-preflight idle exception behavior stays byte-for-byte logically unchanged; strict skip never allows TOOL. Remedy requires verified byte ownership and a supported successful wrapper-observed edit in owning-assignee session, or legitimately finishing/archiving stale peer; declaration/plain unblocking/shell touch are not guarantees. Existing owner guard from prior tasks still applies. Messages must be bounded and shell-safe. This is marked epic-final; full affected runtime/package regression and whole related-epic reporting/landing review are concentrated here. Native Windows gate requires Windows-mounted stable candidate copy, package dependencies/dist and jetbrains-gradle lease, no live shared runtime rebuild.
